a.answer: The original expression is defined exactly for x≠2. Since x²−4=(x−2)(x+2), cancellation gives x+2 on that original domain. The simplified expression x+2 is defined at every real x, including x=2 where it equals 4; therefore it agrees with the original expression wherever the latter is defined, but the two are not equivalent as functions on all real inputs because the original has no value at x=2.

b.answer: For x≠2, x²−4=(x−2)(x+2), so (x²−4)/(x−2)=x+2. The original expression has domain ℝ\{2}. The simplified expression x+2 is defined for every real x, so it is not equivalent to the original at every real number: at x=2 it has value 4 while the original expression is undefined. They agree exactly on ℝ\{2}.
